body:
This is definitely an odd quirk in Godot's physics API, compared to most (all?) other ones I've run into, and something that a lot of people (including myself) learn about the hard way, so I'm generally in favor of improving this in _some_ way.

If I had to guess, the API is likely the way it is to keep things consistent with `add_constant_force`, which similarly takes a global-space offset, and which wouldn't make a whole lot of sense with a global-space position I guess.

If we do decide to go down this route, I would personally prefer to see that the existing methods be "renamed" to `apply_force_at_offset`, `apply_impulse_at_offset` and `add_constant_force_at_offset`, while leaving the existing methods in there, but marked as deprecated. That way it's still not a breaking chance (right now) and we can clearly signal the upcoming breakage for however long we feel is necessary.

Also, you should ideally change this on the 2D side of things as well, which similarly takes an offset currently.

> If we do decide to go down this route, I would personally prefer to see that the existing methods be "renamed" to `apply_force_at_offset`, `apply_impulse_at_offset` and `add_constant_force_at_offset`, while leaving the existing methods in there, but marked as deprecated. That way it's still not a breaking chance (right now) and we can clearly signal the upcoming breakage for however long we feel is necessary.

That's a great idea, it prepares the changes for the future (Godot 5) and alert people of the new functions.

> Also, you should ideally change this on the 2D side of things as well, which similarly takes an offset currently.

Using them in 2D it's not as confusing as in 3D but I agree that it should have the 2D counterpart to keep things in sync. So I'll add those too.
I also forgot that `add_constant_force` takes an offset, but its behavior is a bit different than the apply_force/impulse.
Using a global fixed position for this one would be strange, so I'm not sure if I should also add an `add_constant_force_at_position` or not.
But I agree to rename it to `add_constnat_force_at_offset` to keep things clear and in line with the other renames.

I'll **wait for a while to see how people feel about this change** and implement the changes if they are approved.
Heres a list of changes just keep track later:
- [ ] Add the `...at_position` functions for 2D counterpart
- [ ] Add the deprecated tag to `apply_force/impulse/constant_force`
- [ ] Add renamed `..._at_offset` for `apply_force/apply_impulse/add_constant_force`

> I also forgot that `add_constant_force` takes an offset, but its behavior is a bit different than the apply_force/impulse.
> Using a global fixed position for this one would be strange, so I'm not sure if I should also add an `add_constant_force_at_position` or not.

I don't think a `add_constant_force_at_position` makes much sense, no.

Rebased to remove conflicts. 

And added the parity functions for the 2D physics now. 
Now this **should be complete, and can hopefully be considered to be merged now.**

I don't think we should add the deprecated tag to apply_force/impulse since it seems to be the preferred way to apply central forces still, and it would cause confusion.

Having these  _at_position global alternatives should already solve most of the frustration with using positional forces that users coming to Godot seems to experience due to misunderstanding the local offset position.
